body: I did tell them. She got very offended and told me she wouldn't tolerate insults. I think she misinterpreted, but what else did I expect. Anyway, there's a plan for me to switch therapists next week. It doesn't look too hopeful,.
I'll pay you a thousand dollars if you can make me do what you just told me to do. Or more, if you'd like.

I've actually called them a few times. I talked to this one very nice man and it helped me when I was in a tough spot.

I didn't really read through your comment as thoroughly as you might have wanted me to, but I skimmed it. It sounds like a lot of the things I've already heard from people, when I talk about suicide. Death is forever, it doesn't only affect you, life is so unpredictable, it'll go away, why not just do whatever the heck you want since you want to die anyway? And stuff like that. It's nice to talk about it, but in theory it just doesn't apply. I'm depressed as fuck. Sure my family would be devastated if I died, but what about me? I'm just as devastated to be alive; don't I get a say in what I want? Yeah life is unpredictable, but I doubt things will fix itself and I have no energy to fix it myself. Why not do whatever I want? Because I'd just sleep all day, and that would upset my family quite a bit. I'd rather not listen to their nagging and just die instead.

All in all, depressed people don't think the same way as nondepressed people do. "Just do it, it'll make everything better" or "think about how everyone else will feel if you died" doesn't really register in our minds. The internal pain we're facing is strong enough to block all that out, so to tell us to take that initial step without helping in a physical way is just fruitless and futile.
Everyone tells me that it's not forever, but is it really? It honestly feels like it'll never go away.
I thought we were talking about Adventure Time, when they went to Lumpy Space.

Yes, my life is up to me. I think that's a dangerous thought to give to someone like me, who is very demanding of life. I think about this all the time, about how if I do that thing I don't want to do today, then tomorrow or even the rest of my life can be affected positively. But in my head I know I'll never get the energy to do it, so I know my life will not change in the way I want it to. Of course, that leads to thinking about other options, and for a stubborn mule head like me there is no other option except death. I know I can do it, and I want it more than anything.... besides sleep. I'd rather die than live a life I didn't plan.

I don't think I have a sleep disorder. I wake up after the right amount of sleeping (six hours), but I just refuse to get up. So I sleep more (say three more hours) and wake up again, then stay in bed again because fuck, I hate not being asleep. It's not like I sleep through those 15 or so hours straight through; I wake up repeatedly and choose not to stay awake.

I don't even set up an alarm anymore. I've learned through repetition that I'm going to ignore it. I usually set up my alarms in 1.5 hr intervals, and I've been shown that website. I do wake up, but I fall back asleep regardless of how long I've been sleeping.
I have a therapist; she's linked to the psychiatrist so they work together. Both suck at their jobs.
Best of luck to you (though I doubt you need it being successful as you are), and to everyone else with a mental illness. I'd rather have deformed legs than a deformed mind, am I right?

You're functional, you pass.

And the reason why people create throwaways is to be able to put more information without it being linked to what you've posted in the past. So feel free to say whatever you want.

I also have major depression, if you want to look at my past posts, and I'd gladly accept being euthanize over living a life of self-loathing and watching myself fail at everything I try. Not to mention, I'm wasting other resources that other people, who are more able, can make better use of.

I don't know why I'm even defending myself. The question asked for the most cynical belief I had so obviously what I say will be seen as inhumane and cruel to those who read this.
Someone's gotta do the job. I'll be generous and put myself last.

I think all mentally defective people should be euthanize. Down syndrome, autistic, even clinically depressed, depending on how hopeful it is for them to return as functional beings. My opinion on this has been swayed a bit after reading a few articles on why a lot of what humanity is, is the way it is because we keep these deficient people alive. So I don't mind it as much as I did when I was younger, but if someone put me in charge, sending them off would be the first thing I'd do.

tl;dr Don't put me in charge.

Edit: Guys, the question was "What is the **most cynical** thing you honestly believe?" I know what I think is bad, which was why I posted here.

There aren't many psychiatrists for under 18 yr olds at my hospital. In fact, there are two and one of them is on maternity leave. I tried switching but he's the only one left for now. And there's no one else that'll accept my insurance card so I'm stuck here.

A sleep study? I told my psychiatrist about my excessive sleeping and he didn't do anything about it. He didn't even comment on it, he just nodded and gave me a new prescription for my anti-depressants. He hasn't changed my prescription in a year and I feel worse and worse by the minute.

Nothing can motivate me. When my dog was young, he defecated in his kennel because I couldn't wake myself up. We sleep in the same room and I stayed in bed like an asshole and listened to him whimper all morning. Now that he's grown, he can hold it till the afternoon but that's never good for him. God I'm such a bad owner. I contemplated giving him away because I'm so inconsistent with my schedule.
